_readme: THE EIGHT POINTS A FIRM'S COMPLIANCE PACK IS CHECKED AGAINST (item 4.83, slice 4).
These are section 9 of design/MEETING-REVIEW-DPIA.md, which is the mentor's own published
assessment and the single home of the reasoning behind each one. They live here as data
rather than inside the prompt builder, because CLAUDE.md's hub-page rule is explicit that
content the AI reads must never be hardcoded in a prompt: somebody has to be able to see
it. Every point below is rendered in full on the Compliance tab beside its result.
SECTION 9 HAS NINE POINTS AND THIS FILE HOLDS EIGHT. The ninth -- that the firm has read
and understands the law as it applies to it -- is the DECLARATION, not a document, and it
is the only one Advisor-e asks for. Checking a pack for it would be checking a document
for something no document can carry. The drawing states this in terms.
🔴 THE CHECK READS A DOCUMENT'S NAME, NEVER ITS CONTENTS. design/mockups/compliance-pages.html
says three times that we do not read a firm's documents, and its own examples of a covered
point are file names. A tick means a document APPEARS to address a point, never that it
addresses it adequately -- only the firm's lawyer can say that, and no part of this tells

points.title: That it may lawfully record meetings in its jurisdiction
points.why: The law on recording a conversation is not the same in every country this app is sold into.

points.title: Its reasonable steps under IPP3A — for people discussed but not present
points.why: New Zealand, and in force since 1 May 2026. The software cannot solve this: it cannot know who was mentioned.

points.title: That its staff have been consulted
points.why: Recording employees and reporting on their conduct is monitoring, whoever owns the report.

points.title: How it handles a withdrawal of consent that arrives later
points.why: The software handles a withdrawal during a meeting; one that arrives a week afterwards is the firm's process.

points.title: How it answers a client asking for a copy of their transcript, or its deletion
points.why: The software now serves this through Client Copy Request. A firm still needs its own position on who confirms they are dealing with the right person.

points.title: That it has a privacy breach process
points.why: "As soon as practicable" in New Zealand; 72 hours in the UK and EU.

points.title: That its privacy statement and client engagement terms cover this
points.why: The spoken consent line is not a substitute for a firm's own published position.

points.title: That its deployment is secured
points.why: The server, its access controls, and who at the firm can reach the transcript store. Not a document we can check for — confirm it with whoever runs your servers.
